ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. | `AGENTS.md`   | Working rules for AI agents and contributors                |
| `guidelines/` | General coding, Node, React and UI/UX guidelines (reference) |

## Limits

- Single user, single browser: documents live in localStorage, with no sync or sharing.
- The API is built for local use: it binds to localhost, with an input size cap and a model allowlist, but no per-IP rate limit.
- Markdown can be normalized when it round-trips through the editor.
- Free OpenRouter models have a daily request cap; when it is reached the AI shows as unavailable.

## What I'd do differently with more time

- Run the AI against a real provider contract test in CI instead of fakes only.
- Add browser-level tests (Playwright) for the flows that jsdom cannot cover well, such as selection, focus and popovers.
- Add sync and accounts, then move storage off localStorage.
- Let the user pick the restructure operation (move, split, merge) in the slash menu.

content.text:
Restructure Section no longer makes the AI show as unavailable. The fix is pushed as `65af341`, and `pnpm check` passes. I checked Restructure on a one-paragraph document in the browser; I did not run it on a document with several sections.

**Why it broke**
- **Impossible actions:** on a document with one section, "move" and "merge" have nothing to act on. A "split" needs at least two paragraphs under the heading where your caret is.
- **What the server did:** the model could not return a valid answer, the server retried once and failed validation again, and then returned 503. That 503 sets the global AI status to unavailable, and Ambient waits out its cooldown.
- **What I ruled out:** I called the model directly with a three-section document and it returned valid operations every time. So the model was not the problem.

**The fix**
- The editor now checks the document before asking the AI. If the action cannot apply, you see "This section has nothing to move, split or merge yet." and no API call is made.
- Tests cover the new check for move, merge and split.

**Live check**
- **Slash menu:** it opens.
- **Restructure Section:** on the single-paragraph document it showed the new message, and the status icon stayed on the check.
- **Rewrite Paragraph:** it showed the diff preview.

**If it still fails**
- **What failed:** if "slash commands failing" meant a different item or a different symptom, tell me which one. "Ask What's Missing" is still a disabled "Soon" item.
- **Valid actions:** a restructure that is possible but whose answer the model gets wrong twice still shows as unavailable. I left that as is.

content.text:
The design refinements are done and pushed as `4193eaf`. `pnpm check` passed on two runs (818 tests). An earlier run had one failing test and I never found out which; it did not fail again.

I looked at the editor in dark and light at 800px wide. I did not check 360px, keyboard-only use, or 200% zoom, and the AI underline colour and the other screens (home, history, restructure panel) were not looked at.

**Toggles (your last message)**
- The grouped side-by-side toggles are now two single icon buttons, each switching between two modes.
- **View:** Eye while Visual, SquareCode while Markdown.
- **AI mode:** BotCheck while Ambient, BotOff while On Demand.
- **Press and tooltip:** pressing a button switches to the other mode. The tooltip shows the current mode and the one it switches to, e.g. "Ambient / Switch to On Demand". The accessible name is "Switch to …".

**Brand colour**
- The primary brand colour is now Atlassian purple, built from the ADS purple scale in a new `src/design-system/brand.css`. It overrides only the brand, selected, focus and link tokens, and neutral and semantic colours (success, danger, warning) are unchanged.
- Contrast ratios were calculated, not eyeballed:
  - Filled brand buttons are 8.8:1 (white text on `#673286`) in light mode and 8.1:1 in dark mode.
  - Brand text is 8.8:1 in light mode and 8.1:1 in dark mode.
  - Secondary text is 7.3:1 in light mode and 7.8:1 in dark mode.
- Disabled controls and the input border (3.2:1) are below AAA. The focus ring and the brand border colours are 5.2:1 or 6.0:1.

**Other changes**
- **Type scale:** `src/design-system/typography.css` gives each role one size, weight and line height. Headings in the document body now step down properly, with space above each section.
- **Formatting toolbar:**
  - It sits above the text in the Visual view, one Tab stop, with the arrow keys moving between buttons.
  - Controls: undo, redo, headings 1 to 3, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, bulleted and numbered lists, quote, and code block.
  - Pressed state uses the brand tint, a ring and the icon colour.
  - Link and horizontal rule are not included; a link needs a URL input I did not build.
- **AI pill:**
  - Sparkles icon first, then Rewrite, Fix Tone and Shorten as bordered buttons, then the instruction field and a filled Apply.
  - I left room under the formatting bar so the pill does not cover it. I made that spacing change after my last screenshot, so I did not see the final layout.
- **AI underlines:** every flag kind and the added-word underline in a suggestion now use the brand colour. The kinds still differ by line style (wavy, dashed, dotted, double). The selection tint, the flag chip and the slash menu accent are purple too.

I added tests for the toolbar and updated the toggle tests. The Opus review of the server and editor-plugin changes is still pending.

content.text:
Both are in and pushed as `402b3d4`. `pnpm check` passes (821 tests). I checked the icons and the footer in the browser, in dark mode at about 800px wide.

**Icons**
- **Accept:** check icon. **Dismiss:** X icon.
- They show on the suggestion card, the restructure suggestion, the restructure error panel and the flag panel.
- The flag panel's "View Suggestion" button now has a Sparkles icon and the filled brand style, since it is that panel's main action.
- Button names are unchanged, so screen readers and tests still see "Accept" and "Dismiss".

**Footer**
- It is a thin bar pinned to the bottom of the editor page. It reads "Last edited 1 hour ago · 1 revision", with "revision" singular for one. A document that has not been saved yet shows "Not saved yet · 0 revisions".
- The time and the revision count update after each save. The "last edited" wording only refreshes when the page re-renders, not on a ticking clock.
- Revisions are the entries in the document's history.
- I did not look at it in light mode or at phone width, and I did not check how it behaves on a long document.

I added a small test for the footer.

All three changes are pushed (`a31fe14` and `cdaa6ae`), and `pnpm check` passes with 822 tests. I looked at the editor in the browser. I did not hover every control, and I did not check phone width or the home screen.

- **Footer icons:** the buttons are now 28px with 16px icons, centred in the footer row with 8px padding above and below. The footer's right-hand controls sit closer together.
- **Tooltips:** every icon-only control now shows a Title Case tooltip on hover and keyboard focus.
  - **How it works:** the tooltip is built into the icon button itself, using its label by default ("More actions" shows as "More Actions"). A control whose label contains your own text, like the card delete button (`Delete "…"`), gets that text as its tooltip.
  - **Covered:** the back arrow, the overflow menu, the nav drawer open and close buttons, the bottom-sheet Close button, the card delete buttons, History and the theme switch.
  - **Left edge:** tooltips on controls near the left edge line up with their left side, so they don't run off-screen.
  - **Not covered:** buttons with visible text, like Rewrite or Accept, have no tooltip because the label is already on them.
- **Wide layout:** the full-page layout keeps a side gutter on both sides, 24px on small screens and 32px from md up. In the screenshot the text sits about 22px from the left edge.
- **Extra scrollbar:** the new footer had added a 1px scrollbar to the editor page. I cut the page's bottom padding from 80px to 64px, but I did not reload the page to confirm the scrollbar is gone.

I added a test for the default and custom tooltip text.

# AI Co-Author Editor

A Markdown editor in the browser with an AI co-author. The AI flags passages and suggests rewrites; nothing changes in the document without a visible diff and your explicit Accept.

## Features

- **Home:** list, create, open and delete documents (grid or list).
- **Editor:** Markdown in a rich editor, with a raw Markdown view. Autosave and version history with restore.
- **Ambient mode:** the AI underlines passages (clarity, tone, grammar, questions to the author) after you pause typing. **On Demand mode:** you invoke it on a selection, a section, or with `/`.
- **Suggestions:** an anchored card with a live word diff. Accept, Dismiss or Refine (tone, length, free instruction).
- **Restructure:** move, split or merge sections, with the same preview-then-accept flow.
- **Theme:** light and dark, following the system or set with the toggle.

Documents and history are stored in the browser (localStorage). No account, no database.

## Stack

TypeScript, React, Vite, TipTap (ProseMirror), a small Hono server that proxies AI calls to OpenRouter, Vitest. Reasons and details: [docs/TECHNICAL-DIRECTION.md](docs/TECHNICAL-DIRECTION.md).

## Requirements
| `AGENTS.md`   | Working rules for AI agents and contributors                |
| `guidelines/` | General coding, Node, React and UI/UX guidelines (reference) |

## Limits

- Single user, single browser: documents live in localStorage, with no sync or sharing.
- The API is built for local use: it binds to localhost, with an input size cap and a model allowlist, but no per-IP rate limit.
- Markdown can be normalized when it round-trips through the editor.
- Free OpenRouter models have a daily request cap; when it is reached the AI shows as unavailable.

## What I'd do differently with more time

- Run the AI against a real provider contract test in CI instead of fakes only.
- Add browser-level tests (Playwright) for the flows that jsdom cannot cover well, such as selection, focus and popovers.
- Add sync and accounts, then move storage off localStorage: real data models for documents and history in a database, a migrations setup, and a persistence layer behind the existing storage interface.
- Add more slash actions, including ones focused on code blocks (explain, fix, add comments).
- Export and download a document as a Markdown file.
- Add richer structured logging on the server, with the same redaction rules.
- Add a settings screen to tweak AI options, such as the model per task and the idle pause.
- Add better formatting controls in the editor (bold, italic, lists, links, code) beyond the selection bar.
- Let the user pick the restructure operation (move, split, merge) in the slash menu.

content.content:
**S1. Foundation: Atlassian Design System (ADS) tokens, custom components.** *(Amended 2026-11-17.)*
The look comes from ADS design tokens (color, spacing, typography, radius, elevation, motion). The ADS component packages cannot be used: `@atlaskit/button`, `modal-dialog`, `avatar` and `empty-state` all depend on `@atlaskit/icon`, which S8 bans, and the rest pull in `@compiled/react`, `@emotion` and a feature-gate client. No `@atlaskit/*` package is installed at all. Instead the Apache-2.0 token CSS (light, dark, typography, spacing) is vendored into `src/design-system/vendor/ads-tokens/` with its LICENSE and a note of the source package and version, and every component is custom, plain CSS plus React, in `src/design-system/`. Product-specific AI surfaces (S5) are built the same way, so the whole app reads as one system. Updating the vendored tokens is a deliberate, dated change (S8 re-check).

**S2. Tokens first.**
All color, spacing, typography, radius, elevation and motion values come from the vendored ADS design tokens (S1), exposed as CSS variables. No hard-coded hex or pixel values in feature code. Product-specific values (flag underline, diff insert/delete, restructure accent bar) are defined once as semantic aliases of ADS tokens in `src/design-system/tokens.css`, for example `--ai-flag-underline` and `--ai-diff-insert-bg`.

**S3. Theming: light and dark from day one through tokens.**
ADS theming switches the token set; no component carries its own theme logic. Light is the default (matching the mockup); dark is a token swap with no per-component work.

**S4. Component inventory (mapped from the product record).**
*Amended 2026-11-17: the "Source" column below names the ADS component each custom one is modelled on; none of the `@atlaskit/*` component packages is installed (S1). Each is a custom component in `src/design-system/components/`.*

| Product need | Source |
|---|---|
| Navbar, left menu, disabled items (H2, H3) | ADS primitives + menu/navigation components |
| Buttons (New document, Accept, Dismiss, Refine) | ADS Button |
| Grid / List toggle (H4), Raw Markdown toggle (D15) | ADS toggle / button group |
| Document card and list row (H4) | Custom, ADS primitives + tokens |
| Empty state (H6) | ADS Empty state |
| Delete confirmation (H5) | ADS Modal dialog |
| Tone and Length dropdowns (D6) | ADS Dropdown menu / Select |
| Hover reason tooltip (D2) | ADS Tooltip |

## Where it lives

```
src/design-system/
├── tokens.css          # ADS token import + product semantic aliases + breakpoints (S2, S9)
├── theme.ts            # light/dark switch (S3)
├── responsive/         # useBreakpoint hook, bottom-sheet, drawer (S9)
├── components/         # wrappers over ADS (S4), each with index.ts, types.ts, test
├── ai/                 # custom AI components (S5)
└── icons/              # Icon wrapper, Lucide set + custom SVGs (S6)
scripts/check-licenses.*  # permissive-license allowlist, run by pnpm check (S8)
```

## Open questions (not blocking until the first UI work)

- Final flag-type visual language: color plus underline style per type (D3), to be drawn on the editor mockup.
- Whether ADS typography replaces the system font stack used in the prototype.
- Wordmark and app name; "WebApp" remains the placeholder (H1).

## Phase 2

Visual regression tests for the system, a documented component gallery, density modes, and a brand pass replacing the placeholder name and avatar.

content.content:
One command, `pnpm check`, runs: format check, type-aware strict ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`, license check (S8), Vitest, production build (web and server). **It is created before any feature code.**

- Done only when `pnpm check` passes. Fix causes; never suppress errors or warnings (`@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `any`, non-null `!` need a written reason).
105:- **Disabled controls: the product record wins.** H2 and H3 keep visible, disabled items (a promise of future features); give each a small "Soon" label or tooltip so it explains itself.
106:- Accessibility: semantic HTML first, ARIA only to fill gaps. Everything reachable and operable by keyboard with a visible focus ring; icon-only controls have accessible names; headings and landmarks are hierarchical; async updates use live regions; hover content is also reachable by focus and touch. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

content.text:
The Opus review found one High issue, five Medium and a set of Low ones. I fixed the High, four of the five Mediums and the cheap Lows, and pushed it as `5a897c3`. `pnpm check` passes with 827 tests. I have not re-run anything in the browser since the fixes.

**High, fixed**
- **Formatting toolbar:** keyboard users could not Tab into it. The single Tab stop started on Undo, which is disabled on a fresh document, and a disabled button can't take focus. The Tab stop now lands on the first enabled control, and the arrow keys skip disabled ones. The old test asserted the broken state, so I rewrote it to check the new behaviour.

**Medium**
- **Flags after pause, fixed:** an Ambient call already in flight could still show flags after you switched to On Demand or the Markdown view. It still finishes and caches, but no longer shows flags once paused.
- **Tooltip text, fixed:** the tooltip description is now attached to the button itself, so screen readers hear it. The current mode (for example Ambient) is still only in the tooltip. Touch users still cannot see it, because the icon shows the target mode.
- **Footer button size, fixed:** the 28px buttons no longer apply on touch screens, which keep the 44px size.
- **D4 amendment, fixed:** D4 in `docs/PRODUCT-DIRECTION.md` now says an idle pause of 5 seconds by default (set by `VITE_AI_IDLE_PAUSE_SECONDS`), dated 2026-11-18.
- **Retry comment, not fixed:** the retry code has one wake slot, so the latest held paragraph is retried when the cooldown ends and any others wait for a new edit. I corrected the comment but left the behaviour as is. The retry count stays bounded, as the review confirmed.

**Low, fixed**
- **Title Case:** minor words (to, of, the) stay lowercase, so "Switch to Light Theme" matches your style. Accents and apostrophes are no longer mangled. I added a test.
- **Export:** the download link is released a second later, because some browsers cancel the download if it is released immediately.
- **`/api/info`:** the response now goes through `ServerInfoSchema`, and the model-names fetch has a 5-second timeout.
- **Imports:** two deep `@shared/schemas/...` imports now use the index.
- **Brand colour:** the dark-theme pressed tint is deeper, so brand text on it passes the 4.5:1 minimum (5.07:1). I did not use the 7:1 value for dark mode.
- **Messages:** the restructure message says what is possible: move and merge need two sections, split needs two paragraphs. A comment and a debt note were updated too.

**Left alone**
- **`EditorForm.tsx`:** it is 268 lines, over the ~200-line split rule.
- **Identical paragraphs:** when two paragraphs have identical text, only the first gets flags.
- **Weak test:** one test, for a range selection making no call, would pass even if a call were scheduled.
- **Not checked by the reviewer:**
  - It did not run `pnpm check`, a browser or a screen reader.
  - It could not check whether every configured OpenRouter model accepts the reasoning setting.
  - It could not run Node.
  - Three areas I named (Popover, the current-line extension, the theme controller) were outside the commit range it reviewed and were not covered.

I can do the `EditorForm.tsx` split, the duplicate-paragraph fix and the stronger test as one more round.

content.text:
The remaining round is pushed as `d28cad9`, and `pnpm check` passes (827 tests). I did not re-check it in the browser. I made two of the three items; the duplicate-paragraph fix is not in.

- **`EditorForm.tsx` split:** the Visual/Markdown switching and the export logic moved into a new hook, `useMarkdownView.ts`. The form is now 241 lines instead of 268. That is still over the ~200 target, but the remaining code is page wiring.
- **Range-selection test:** the old test could never fail. The stronger version advances time by a second, so a call sent for leaving a paragraph would be caught. I could not wait past the idle pause. The test inserts text as its setup, which counts as an edit, so after the idle pause the app legitimately sends a call for that edited paragraph. One second is enough to catch a leave-triggered call, which goes out at once.
- **Identical paragraphs (not fixed):** I tried giving flags to every paragraph with the same text, but it broke the Dismiss test. Dismiss clears only one flag, so the copy on the other paragraph stayed behind. I reverted it and left a `DEBT:` note in `useFlagAnalysis.ts`. A real fix needs per-paragraph flag identity, so for now only the first of two identical paragraphs is flagged.

Every Opus finding is now fixed, or documented where I chose not to change the behaviour.

The formatting toolbar now floats at the bottom of the screen, with a gap above the footer. The change is pushed as `cd25d7e` and `pnpm check` passes.

I checked it in the browser. At the top of a 41-paragraph document the toolbar sits at the bottom of the screen, and at the end of the page there is clear space under the last paragraph. After that screenshot I added the page-colour fill for the gap, so I have not seen it in the browser.

- **Position:** the toolbar sits 16px above the footer. The page now has extra bottom padding, so the last paragraph can scroll fully clear of it.
- **Footer height:** the footer has a fixed height (a new `--app-footer-height` variable), which is what the toolbar's offset is measured from.
- **Tooltips:** the toolbar's tooltips open upward so the footer does not cover them.
- **Selection bubble:** it now avoids the bottom bars instead of the top, so it should not land under the toolbar. I did not test that either.
- **Text passing beneath:** scrolled text still passes beneath the toolbar, which is the nature of a floating bar. The new fill hides text in the gap between the toolbar and the footer.

content.text:
The AI bubble, the toolbar fix and the README additions are all pushed. `pnpm check` passes (831 tests) for the first two; the README commit only changed Markdown, which Prettier accepts.

**Toolbar:** it is now only as wide as its controls and centred in the column, with no empty space on the right.

**AI bubble:** this is a new design-system component, `AiBubble`.
- **Where it sits:** it appears in the right margin of a paragraph, level with its first line. Paragraphs reserve that space, so text never shifts.
- **Loading:** while the AI is analyzing a paragraph, a round bubble with a sparkle icon and a spinning ring shows, announced to screen readers as "AI Is Analyzing This Paragraph".
- **Ready:** once the paragraph's flags are underlined, the bubble pulses softly. It shows a count when there is more than one suggestion. Clicking it opens the suggestion card for the first flag.
- **Motion:** it uses only fade, scale and rotate, and respects reduced motion.
- **Live check:** I saw the loading bubble, the underline and the pulsing bubble, and clicking it opened the Clarity card.
- **One failed call:** the first call returned a 503. A direct request moments later worked, so it looks like a transient provider error. The scheduler retried after the 30-second cooldown and succeeded.
- **Tests:** the bubble has component tests, and the scheduler has a new test for the loading signal.

**README**
- **New "How it was built" section:** it recaps the three stages. Discovery: product interviews turned into written decisions. Implementation: small tasks from a board, built one at a time on `development` with the full check on each change. Polish: refinement from using and reviewing the running app.
- **"More time" list:** it now includes using the development lifecycle more fully, with issues, a branch per change, reviewed pull requests with CI, and tagged releases with a changelog.
- **Features list:** it also mentions the AI bubble.

I did not check the bubble in light mode, at phone width, or in a document with several flagged paragraphs.

content.text:
The AI bubble looks right in light mode and at 360px. The toolbar now has a brand-colour outline. It's pushed as `7c284a6` and `pnpm check` passes (831 tests).

**Toolbar outline:** the container border is now the brand purple. I saw it in light mode at desktop width.

**AI bubble, light mode:** the ready bubble shows on the right of the paragraph, with the "2" count badge for two suggestions. The underlines are wavy brand purple. I could only see the bubble small in the screenshot, so I did not judge the pulse animation itself.

**AI bubble, 360px:**
- **Bubble:** it sits in the right margin with the count badge and does not touch the text.
- **Card:** tapping it opened the suggestion card as a bottom sheet, with Clarity, "View Suggestion" and "Dismiss".
- **Tap mapping:** my first taps missed because the emulated phone viewport maps tap coordinates to the wrong place. With corrected coordinates a real tap worked, so that was a testing problem, not an app bug.

**Fix at 360px:** the formatting toolbar wrapped into three tall rows and covered about 150px of the screen. Below 768px it is now one row that scrolls sideways, so the toolbar is a single row at the bottom. I saw it, but I did not scroll it sideways to reach the controls at the far end.

I did not check dark mode at 360px, or the footer at 360px.

content.text:
I took four screenshots, added them in a new `screenshots/` folder, and put a "Preview" section with them at the top of the README. It is pushed as `1bb5c9b`. I did not re-run `pnpm check` for the README change.

The screenshots, all from the editor with your current document's text:
- **`home.jpg`:** the document grid in light mode.
- **`editor-ambient.jpg`:** light mode, with the wavy underlines and the AI bubble showing "2".
- **`suggestion-card.jpg`:** the suggestion card with the live word diff, and the Accept, Dismiss and Refine controls.
- **`editor-dark-selection.jpg`:** dark theme, with the selection bar (sparkle, Rewrite, Fix Tone, Shorten and the instruction field).

They are 800×500 JPEGs, which is all the in-app browser pane captures, so they are smaller than a true 1280px screenshot. The home screenshot also shows a second "Untitled document" card, a test document I made with filler paragraphs. # AGENTS.md

Working rules for AI agents and people in this repo. **Draft: this will evolve as the product grows.** If a rule is wrong or in the way, say so and propose a change instead of working around it.

Priority: user instruction > this file and `docs/` > `guidelines/`. `Never` = hard rule. The full general guidelines are in `guidelines/` (CODING, NODEJS, REACT, UIUX); this file is the project-adapted distillation. **Do not read `guidelines/` by default**; open one only when this file is silent on something.

## Project in one paragraph

A browser-based Markdown editor where an AI co-author flags and suggests; the user always sees a diff and must Accept. React + Vite + TipTap front end, a small Hono proxy to OpenRouter, localStorage persistence, no auth, no database. Setup and commands: `README.md`.

## Source of truth

Read only what the task needs, not everything.

| Need | File |
|---|---|
| What the product does (D1-D17 editor, H1-H7 home) | `docs/PRODUCT-DIRECTION.md` |
| Stack, AI contract, storage, security, structure, packages, gates (T1-T13) | `docs/TECHNICAL-DIRECTION.md` |
| Tokens, components, licenses, responsive (S1-S9) | `docs/DESIGN-DIRECTION.md` |

Product decisions are settled. Do not re-open them; if code contradicts one, flag it. Cite decision IDs (`D4`, `H5`, `T7`, `S8`) in code comments and test names.

## Project rules

1. **Nothing changes the document without Accept** (T3). Suggestions are decorations; Accept is one transaction.
2. **Contracts live in `shared/schemas/`** as zod, types from `z.infer` (T11). Never hand-duplicate a type.
3. **The OpenRouter key never reaches the browser** (T4). Model names come from config, never from the client (T7).
4. **Model output is untrusted** (T10): validate with zod, render as text only, drop responses whose paragraph hash no longer matches.
5. **Feature code imports UI only from `src/design-system/`**, never `@atlaskit/*` or icon packages directly (S8).
6. **Only permissive licenses** (Apache-2.0, MIT, ISC, BSD). `@atlaskit/icon` and `@atlaskit/logo` are banned; icons are Lucide or custom SVG (S6, S8).
7. **No hover-only affordances**; every interaction has a touch and keyboard path (S9, D17).
8. **No test calls the real model** (T9). Never commit `.env` or secrets. Never log document text or the API key.

## The gate

One command, `pnpm check`, runs: format check, type-aware strict ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`, license check (S8), Vitest, production build (web and server). **It is created before any feature code.**

- Done only when `pnpm check` passes. Fix causes; never suppress errors or warnings (`@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `any`, non-null `!` need a written reason).
- After every change run the fast checks (format, lint, types). Run tests by scope: affected tests per step, the full suite once before push or done.
- ESLint errors on: undeclared and unused names, shadowing, floating promises, explicit `any`, missing types, `react-hooks` violations, deep imports across features, direct `@atlaskit/*` imports. No `console.log` left behind.
- Report what was run and the real result. Never claim unverified work passes.

## Packages (T12)

- **pnpm only.** Never npm or yarn; never commit another lockfile. Commands: `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`.
- **Exact versions only.** `.npmrc` has `save-exact=true`. No `^`, `~`, ranges or `latest`, dev dependencies included. `packageManager` and `engines` pin pnpm and Node.
- Commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`; install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Adding a dependency: first prefer the platform, the standard library or code we already have. Verify the exact name exists and is maintained, check its license (S8), add one package at a time, run `pnpm check`, commit alone.
- Upgrading: deliberate, one package at a time, license re-checked, checks run, committed alone. `pnpm audit` shows no high or critical findings.
- Dependency install scripts stay blocked unless explicitly allowlisted with a reason.
- Wrap third-party libraries in an adapter when they touch domain logic (AI provider, storage, design system).

## Coding rules

- Read related files before editing; match existing patterns, naming and style. Take the first option that works: not needed -> reuse -> standard library -> platform feature -> installed dependency -> small edit -> new minimal code.
- Smallest diff that fully solves the task. Never refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code. Before changing a signature or schema, find and update every caller.
- Never leave TODOs, stubs, mock data, dead code, commented-out code or debug output. A deliberate shortcut gets one `DEBT:` comment with its limit and when to revisit.
- Never invent APIs, flags or package names; verify in the repo, lockfile or docs. Never deprecated APIs.
- Bug: reproduce it, fix the root cause, not the symptom. Stuck after two attempts at the same fix: stop, report what failed, propose options.
- Ambiguous requirement: pick the simplest option and state the assumption.
- KISS, YAGNI. Abstract on the third repetition; duplication beats a wrong abstraction. One responsibility per function and module. Pure core, side effects at the edges. Composition over inheritance.
- Functions: one level of abstraction, guard clauses over nesting (at most ~3 levels), at most ~4 parameters, no boolean flag parameters, no hidden inputs or outputs.
- Names state intent; units in the name (`timeout_ms`); no magic numbers or strings. No `utils`/`helpers` dumping grounds: name modules by what they own (`diff`, `hash`).
- Types: strictest checking, no escape hatches. Parse external data at the boundary (API, storage, environment) into validated types, then trust them. Discriminated unions instead of flag combinations; `as const` objects instead of `enum`; immutable by default.
- Errors: never swallow (no empty `catch`). Expected failures are typed results; exceptions are for bugs. Messages state what failed, without secrets. Handle edges: empty, missing, zero, duplicate, non-ASCII.
- Never global mutable state or side effects at import time. Inject IO, clock, randomness and environment at the edges; wrap `window`, `localStorage` and the clock in a module or hook.
- Whatever a scope acquires (listener, timer, request, subscription) the same scope releases, on every path.
- Bound everything: input size, retries, timeouts, caches. Measure before optimizing.
- Comments explain why, not what. Document public APIs: purpose, inputs, errors.

## Frontend rules (React)

- Feature-first per T11: components (UI) / hooks (logic) / API client (IO). Never `fetch` in a component. One component per file; split files over ~200 lines. Never define a component inside another.
- Import direction: `app -> features -> design-system / lib`. Other features are reached only through their `index.ts`.
- TypeScript `strict` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. No `as` casts to silence errors, no `React.FC`. Variants and async state (idle, loading, ready, error) are discriminated unions.
- State at the lowest scope that works: local -> lifted -> URL -> context -> Zustand. Derive values in render; never mirror props or derived data in state. Editor-internal state belongs to the ProseMirror plugins (T3), not React state.
- Effects only synchronize with external systems and always have full deps and cleanup. Never use effects for derived state, event logic or fetching. Reset with `key`. No `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo` by default; add after profiling.
- AI calls go through the typed client in `features/ai`: timeout, abort `signal` on every request, one normalized error shape. Handle loading, error, empty and success. AI failure shows the D14 status and never breaks the editor.
- Stable `key` from ids, never the index. Never render `count && <X />`. Dates, numbers and relative times through `Intl`.
- Error boundary per route and around the editor, with fallback and retry. Boundaries do not catch event-handler or async errors; handle those where they occur.
- Security: never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; never render user, API or LLM content as HTML or Markdown without sanitizing (T10). No secrets in client code. External `target="_blank"` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. No inline scripts, `eval` or `new Function`.
- Route-level `lazy` + `Suspense`; check bundle cost before adding a library.
- Tests: Vitest + React Testing Library + `user-event`, colocated as `Component.test.tsx`. Query by role, label or text (`data-testid` last). Never test internal state or class names. `findBy*`/`waitFor` and fake timers (for the D4 pause; use `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })`, or `findBy*` can hang), never fixed sleeps. A src test that needs the DOM is a `.tsx` file (jsdom project). The AI is faked at the client boundary. Cover loading, error, empty and success.

## Server rules (Hono, Node)

- ESM only. Layers: route (thin) -> AI service -> `AIProvider`. Request and response objects never enter the service. The app is built by a factory with its dependencies passed in (`createApp(deps)`); a separate entrypoint listens.
- Validate body, params and query with zod at the boundary, reject unknown fields, and serialize responses through schemas (T5).
- Environment is parsed once at startup into a typed config; never read `process.env` elsewhere (T7). Fail fast on missing config.
- One error handler maps typed errors to status codes with one body shape; never send stack traces. Out-of-credit maps to the D14 status.
- Every outbound call has a timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout`) and is cancelled when the client disconnects. Retries are bounded (T5: one).
- Never block the event loop: no `*Sync` calls on request paths. Every promise is awaited or handled; `return await` inside `try`.
- Body size limit and model allowlist enforced here (T7). CORS: same-origin through the Vite proxy; allow only the local dev origin.
- Structured logs to stdout with secrets and document text redacted. Never `eval`, `new Function` or `vm`.
- Tests: the service is unit-tested with a fake `AIProvider`; routes through Hono's in-process request against the factory app. Tests close what they open.

## UI/UX rules

- **Done means seen.** Every screen is looked at rendered (screenshot in the browser pane), not only read as code. Check at 360, 768 and 1280px, light and dark, keyboard only, and 200% zoom. Accessibility check clean once automated (axe or similar); until then a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass. Contrast meets WCAG AA.
- Every data view has loading, empty, error and success states (H6, D14).
- Heuristics that matter here: visible system status (feedback in 100 ms, progress after 1 s, e.g. the card spinner); user control (Accept, Dismiss, Esc, single-step undo D17); error prevention (destructive actions confirm and name the object, H5); recovery (say what happened and how to fix, keep the user's input); consistency (reuse design-system components, never restyle one-off); minimal (one primary action per screen).
- Layout: spacing, sizes and radii from tokens only (S2). No horizontal scroll at 320px; fully usable from 360px (S9). Document text at least 16px with 45-75 characters per line; UI chrome follows the ADS scale. Touch targets at least 44x44 on coarse pointers. Reserve space for async content so layout never shifts.
- Color: semantic tokens only, never raw hex; the brand is Atlassian purple (`brand.css`), so use the brand tokens, not blue; never color alone to carry meaning (S7). Hover, focus, active, selected, disabled and error states are visibly distinct.
- Buttons act, links navigate; button labels are verbs naming the outcome. Modals are rare (delete confirm only): focus trapped, `Esc` closes, focus returns to the trigger. No toast as the only place an error appears.
- **Disabled controls: the product record wins.** H2 and H3 keep visible, disabled items (a promise of future features); give each a small "Soon" label or tooltip so it explains itself.
- Accessibility: semantic HTML first, ARIA only to fill gaps. Everything reachable and operable by keyboard with a visible focus ring; icon-only controls have accessible names and a Title Case tooltip (`IconButton` adds it); headings and landmarks are hierarchical; async updates use live regions; hover content is also reachable by focus and touch. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Motion explains cause and effect: 150-300 ms, transform and opacity only, never blocking input.
- Content: plain language, one term per concept. Labels (buttons, menu items, toggles, headings, titles) use Title Case ("Fix Tone", "Go to Home"); messages, notes and placeholders stay in sentence case. The user chose this over the prototype's sentence case. The AI speaks in neutral, factual one-liners (D8). Never put a placeholder where a label belongs.

## Dropped on purpose (does not fit this project yet)

Revisit when the product grows (Phase 2: sign-in, sync, real users).

- **Server:** PostgreSQL and the data layer, migrations, idempotency keys, durable job queues, authentication and authorization (JWT, passwords, sessions, cookies), multi-instance concerns (shared rate-limit store, trusted proxies, readiness and graceful shutdown), containers and non-root runtime, Fastify and pino defaults (we use Hono), profiling and `AsyncLocalStorage` practice.
- **Frontend:** TanStack Query and its key and mutation rules, React Hook Form, Tailwind, Next.js, auth tokens, virtualization, live connections, i18n and message catalogs, MSW (the AI is faked at our own boundary).
- **UI/UX:** A/B testing, HEART and SUS metrics, scheduled user-testing rounds, native-platform guidance, tables, search, multi-step forms, password rules, Core Web Vitals targets, right-to-left and translation stress tests, consent and dark-pattern rules, media captions.
- **General:** money and time-zone rules, thread-safety rules.

## Agent roles and models

| Role | Model | Does | Does not |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator** | Sonnet | Talks to the user, splits work, writes handoff briefs, integrates results, runs `pnpm check`, owns commits | Large implementations itself; design-heavy planning |
| **Planner / Reviewer** | Opus | Plans non-trivial or cross-cutting work; reviews diffs against these rules and the decision IDs | Write the implementation; run long builds |
| **Builder** | Haiku | Implements one well-bounded task from a brief; writes its tests | Make design decisions, change contracts, touch files outside its brief |

Flow per change: Orchestrator -> (Opus plan, if needed) -> Haiku build -> orchestrator runs the scoped checks (format, lint, types, tests of the touched folders) -> commit and push. No per-phase Opus review and no per-phase browser pass.

Checkpoints (a milestone, or the end of a parallel set): one full `pnpm check`, one Opus review of everything since the last checkpoint (mandatory for `shared/`, `server/` and editor plugins, and always before the first live key use), and one browser pass at 360, 768 and 1280px, light and dark. Findings become one fix round. Run builds, reviews and browser checks in the background while the next phase is built.

Escalate instead of guessing: a builder that hits an ambiguity, a contract change or a rule conflict stops and reports to the orchestrator.

## Agent reuse (cache-friendly)

- **One long-lived builder per area** (editor, server, design system), continued with `SendMessage` instead of a new spawn. A resumed agent keeps its read files and the prompt cache; a cold start pays them again.
- **Batch related phases into one brief** for the same builder when they touch the same area, instead of one agent per phase. Spawn a new agent only for a new area or when the old context is stale or too large.
- **One Opus reviewer per checkpoint**, resumed for later checkpoints. Brief it with the commit range, not file lists.
- Keep briefs short and point to files; check the usage report after each checkpoint and cut what re-reads the same files.

## Handoffs: cold starts and token efficiency

Side agents start with **no memory of the conversation**. Every handoff carries exactly what they need and nothing more.

**Orchestrator, when handing off:**
- Pass **file paths and decision IDs, not pasted contents.** The agent reads what it needs.
- Name the **minimum reading list** (usually 1-3 files plus the relevant IDs). Never tell a builder to read all of `docs/` or `guidelines/`; the rules a builder needs are in this file.
- State the **scope as a whitelist of files** it may create or edit, and what is out of bounds.
- Give **checkable acceptance criteria** (a test passes, `pnpm check` is green, a specific behavior).
- One task per brief, small enough to finish in one pass. Split large work into independent briefs with no shared files, each step building and passing checks before the next.
- Ask for a **short, structured return** so the result is cheap to read back.

**Brief template:**

```
Task: <one sentence>
Why: <decision IDs, e.g. D4, T5>
Read first: <paths, max ~3>
May edit/create: <file whitelist>
Do not touch: <paths or areas>
Done when: <checkable criteria; include `pnpm check` green>
Return: files changed, one line per change, anything unresolved. No code dumps.
```

**Builder, on start:** read the brief, then only the listed files; do not explore the repo or re-read docs unless told. Follow neighboring patterns. Do not widen scope; note adjacent problems in the return instead of fixing them. Run `pnpm check` before returning and report failures verbatim and briefly.

**Reviewer (Opus), on start:** receive the diff and the decision IDs it should satisfy, not the history. Check against these rules and the cited IDs; report findings ranked by severity with file and line. Do not rewrite code.

**Return format (all side agents):**

```
Status: done | blocked | partial
Changed: <path>: <what, one line>
Checks: <pnpm check result>
Open: <questions, risks, follow-ups>
```

## Context hygiene

- Keep this file and the briefs short; long context costs tokens on every cold start.
- Record durable decisions in `docs/` (with an ID), not in chat. A decision that exists only in a conversation is lost to the next agent.
- When a rule here changes, update this file in the same change.

## Git

Work on `development`; `main` is for releases. Short, imperative commit messages. One commit per change; update any doc the change touches. Add one dependency or one upgrade per commit. The raw AI session files in `ai-sessions/` are added last, unedited except for masked secrets, as the brief requires.

- [Dev environment: Lima VM](dev-environment-lima.md) — user codes in a Lima VM; no Node/pnpm on host, keep out of docs
- [Review cadence](review-cadence-checkpoints.md) — batch Opus review, full gate, browser checks at milestones
- [Agent reuse](agent-reuse-cache-friendly.md) — SendMessage long-lived agents, batch phases, avoid cold starts

One command, `pnpm check`, runs: format check, type-aware strict ESLint, `tsc --noEmit`, license check (S8), Vitest, production build (web and server). **It is created before any feature code.**

- Done only when `pnpm check` passes. Fix causes; never suppress errors or warnings (`@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable`, `any`, non-null `!` need a written reason).
- After every change run the fast checks (format, lint, types). Run tests by scope: affected tests per step, the full suite once before push or done.
- ESLint errors on: undeclared and unused names, shadowing, floating promises, explicit `any`, missing types, `react-hooks` violations, deep imports across features, direct `@atlaskit/*` imports. No `console.log` left behind.
- Report what was run and the real result. Never claim unverified work passes.

## Packages (T12)

- **pnpm only.** Never npm or yarn; never commit another lockfile. Commands: `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm check`.
- **Exact versions only.** `.npmrc` has `save-exact=true`. No `^`, `~`, ranges or `latest`, dev dependencies included. `packageManager` and `engines` pin pnpm and Node.
- Commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`; install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
- Adding a dependency: first prefer the platform, the standard library or code we already have. Verify the exact name exists and is maintained, check its license (S8), add one package at a time, run `pnpm check`, commit alone.
- Upgrading: deliberate, one package at a time, license re-checked, checks run, committed alone. `pnpm audit` shows no high or critical findings.
- Dependency install scripts stay blocked unless explicitly allowlisted with a reason.
- Wrap third-party libraries in an adapter when they touch domain logic (AI provider, storage, design system).

## Coding rules

- Read related files before editing; match existing patterns, naming and style. Take the first option that works: not needed -> reuse -> standard library -> platform feature -> installed dependency -> small edit -> new minimal code.
- Smallest diff that fully solves the task. Never refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code. Before changing a signature or schema, find and update every caller.
- Never leave TODOs, stubs, mock data, dead code, commented-out code or debug output. A deliberate shortcut gets one `DEBT:` comment with its limit and when to revisit.
- Never invent APIs, flags or package names; verify in the repo, lockfile or docs. Never deprecated APIs.
- Bug: reproduce it, fix the root cause, not the symptom. Stuck after two attempts at the same fix: stop, report what failed, propose options.
- Ambiguous requirement: pick the simplest option and state the assumption.
- KISS, YAGNI. Abstract on the third repetition; duplication beats a wrong abstraction. One responsibility per function and module. Pure core, side effects at the edges. Composition over inheritance.
- Functions: one level of abstraction, guard clauses over nesting (at most ~3 levels), at most ~4 parameters, no boolean flag parameters, no hidden inputs or outputs.
- Names state intent; units in the name (`timeout_ms`); no magic numbers or strings. No `utils`/`helpers` dumping grounds: name modules by what they own (`diff`, `hash`).
- Types: strictest checking, no escape hatches. Parse external data at the boundary (API, storage, environment) into validated types, then trust them. Discriminated unions instead of flag combinations; `as const` objects instead of `enum`; immutable by default.
- Errors: never swallow (no empty `catch`). Expected failures are typed results; exceptions are for bugs. Messages state what failed, without secrets. Handle edges: empty, missing, zero, duplicate, non-ASCII.
- Never global mutable state or side effects at import time. Inject IO, clock, randomness and environment at the edges; wrap `window`, `localStorage` and the clock in a module or hook.
- Whatever a scope acquires (listener, timer, request, subscription) the same scope releases, on every path.
- Bound everything: input size, retries, timeouts, caches. Measure before optimizing.
- Comments explain why, not what. Document public APIs: purpose, inputs, errors.

## Frontend rules (React)

- Feature-first per T11: components (UI) / hooks (logic) / API client (IO). Never `fetch` in a component. One component per file; split files over ~200 lines. Never define a component inside another.
- Import direction: `app -> features -> design-system / lib`. Other features are reached only through their `index.ts`.
- TypeScript `strict` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. No `as` casts to silence errors, no `React.FC`. Variants and async state (idle, loading, ready, error) are discriminated unions.
- State at the lowest scope that works: local -> lifted -> URL -> context -> Zustand. Derive values in render; never mirror props or derived data in state. Editor-internal state belongs to the ProseMirror plugins (T3), not React state.
- Effects only synchronize with external systems and always have full deps and cleanup. Never use effects for derived state, event logic or fetching. Reset with `key`. No `useMemo`/`useCallback`/`memo` by default; add after profiling.
- AI calls go through the typed client in `features/ai`: timeout, abort `signal` on every request, one normalized error shape. Handle loading, error, empty and success. AI failure shows the D14 status and never breaks the editor.
- Stable `key` from ids, never the index. Never render `count && <X />`. Dates, numbers and relative times through `Intl`.
- Error boundary per route and around the editor, with fallback and retry. Boundaries do not catch event-handler or async errors; handle those where they occur.
- Security: never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; never render user, API or LLM content as HTML or Markdown without sanitizing (T10). No secrets in client code. External `target="_blank"` gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. No inline scripts, `eval` or `new Function`.
- Route-level `lazy` + `Suspense`; check bundle cost before adding a library.
- Tests: Vitest + React Testing Library + `user-event`, colocated as `Component.test.tsx`. Query by role, label or text (`data-testid` last). Never test internal state or class names. `findBy*`/`waitFor` and fake timers (for the D4 pause; use `vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true })` with `userEvent.setup({ advanceTimers: vi.advanceTimersByTime })`, or `findBy*` can hang), never fixed sleeps. A src test that needs the DOM is a `.tsx` file (jsdom project). The AI is faked at the client boundary. Cover loading, error, empty and success.

## Server rules (Hono, Node)

- ESM only. Layers: route (thin) -> AI service -> `AIProvider`. Request and response objects never enter the service. The app is built by a factory with its dependencies passed in (`createApp(deps)`); a separate entrypoint listens.
- Validate body, params and query with zod at the boundary, reject unknown fields, and serialize responses through schemas (T5).
- Environment is parsed once at startup into a typed config; never read `process.env` elsewhere (T7). Fail fast on missing config.
- One error handler maps typed errors to status codes with one body shape; never send stack traces. Out-of-credit maps to the D14 status.
- Every outbound call has a timeout (`AbortSignal.timeout`) and is cancelled when the client disconnects. Retries are bounded (T5: one).
- Never block the event loop: no `*Sync` calls on request paths. Every promise is awaited or handled; `return await` inside `try`.
- Body size limit and model allowlist enforced here (T7). CORS: same-origin through the Vite proxy; allow only the local dev origin.
- Structured logs to stdout with secrets and document text redacted. Never `eval`, `new Function` or `vm`.
- Tests: the service is unit-tested with a fake `AIProvider`; routes through Hono's in-process request against the factory app. Tests close what they open.

## UI/UX rules

- **Done means seen.** Every screen is looked at rendered (screenshot in the browser pane), not only read as code. Check at 360, 768 and 1280px, light and dark, keyboard only, and 200% zoom. Accessibility check clean once automated (axe or similar); until then a manual keyboard and screen-reader pass. Contrast meets WCAG AA.
- Every data view has loading, empty, error and success states (H6, D14).
- Heuristics that matter here: visible system status (feedback in 100 ms, progress after 1 s, e.g. the card spinner); user control (Accept, Dismiss, Esc, single-step undo D17); error prevention (destructive actions confirm and name the object, H5); recovery (say what happened and how to fix, keep the user's input); consistency (reuse design-system components, never restyle one-off); minimal (one primary action per screen).
- Layout: spacing, sizes and radii from tokens only (S2). No horizontal scroll at 320px; fully usable from 360px (S9). Document text at least 16px with 45-75 characters per line; UI chrome follows the ADS scale. Touch targets at least 44x44 on coarse pointers. Reserve space for async content so layout never shifts.
- Color: semantic tokens only, never raw hex; the brand is Atlassian purple (`brand.css`), so use the brand tokens, not blue; never color alone to carry meaning (S7). Hover, focus, active, selected, disabled and error states are visibly distinct.
- Buttons act, links navigate; button labels are verbs naming the outcome. Modals are rare (delete confirm only): focus trapped, `Esc` closes, focus returns to the trigger. No toast as the only place an error appears.
- **Disabled controls: the product record wins.** H2 and H3 keep visible, disabled items (a promise of future features); give each a small "Soon" label or tooltip so it explains itself.
- Accessibility: semantic HTML first, ARIA only to fill gaps. Everything reachable and operable by keyboard with a visible focus ring; icon-only controls have accessible names and a Title Case tooltip (`IconButton` adds it); headings and landmarks are hierarchical; async updates use live regions; hover content is also reachable by focus and touch. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Motion explains cause and effect: 150-300 ms, transform and opacity only, never blocking input.
- Content: plain language, one term per concept. Labels (buttons, menu items, toggles, headings, titles) use Title Case ("Fix Tone", "Go to Home"); messages, notes and placeholders stay in sentence case. The user chose this over the prototype's sentence case. The AI speaks in neutral, factual one-liners (D8). Never put a placeholder where a label belongs.

## Dropped on purpose (does not fit this project yet)

Revisit when the product grows (Phase 2: sign-in, sync, real users).

- **Server:** PostgreSQL and the data layer, migrations, idempotency keys, durable job queues, authentication and authorization (JWT, passwords, sessions, cookies), multi-instance concerns (shared rate-limit store, trusted proxies, readiness and graceful shutdown), containers and non-root runtime, Fastify and pino defaults (we use Hono), profiling and `AsyncLocalStorage` practice.
- **Frontend:** TanStack Query and its key and mutation rules, React Hook Form, Tailwind, Next.js, auth tokens, virtualization, live connections, i18n and message catalogs, MSW (the AI is faked at our own boundary).
- **UI/UX:** A/B testing, HEART and SUS metrics, scheduled user-testing rounds, native-platform guidance, tables, search, multi-step forms, password rules, Core Web Vitals targets, right-to-left and translation stress tests, consent and dark-pattern rules, media captions.
- **General:** money and time-zone rules, thread-safety rules.

## Agent roles and models

| Role | Model | Does | Does not |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Orchestrator** | Sonnet | Talks to the user, splits work, writes handoff briefs, integrates results, runs `pnpm check`, owns commits | Large implementations itself; design-heavy planning |
| **Planner / Reviewer** | Opus | Plans non-trivial or cross-cutting work; reviews diffs against these rules and the decision IDs | Write the implementation; run long builds |
| **Builder** | Haiku | Implements one well-bounded task from a brief; writes its tests | Make design decisions, change contracts, touch files outside its brief |

Flow per change: Orchestrator -> (Opus plan, if needed) -> Haiku build -> orchestrator runs the scoped checks (format, lint, types, tests of the touched folders) -> commit and push. No per-phase Opus review and no per-phase browser pass.

Checkpoints (a milestone, or the end of a parallel set): one full `pnpm check`, one Opus review of everything since the last checkpoint (mandatory for `shared/`, `server/` and editor plugins, and always before the first live key use), and one browser pass at 360, 768 and 1280px, light and dark. Findings become one fix round. Run builds, reviews and browser checks in the background while the next phase is built.

Escalate instead of guessing: a builder that hits an ambiguity, a contract change or a rule conflict stops and reports to the orchestrator.

## Agent reuse (cache-friendly)

- **One long-lived builder per area** (editor, server, design system), continued with `SendMessage` instead of a new spawn. A resumed agent keeps its read files and the prompt cache; a cold start pays them again.
- **Batch related phases into one brief** for the same builder when they touch the same area, instead of one agent per phase. Spawn a new agent only for a new area or when the old context is stale or too large.
- **One Opus reviewer per checkpoint**, resumed for later checkpoints. Brief it with the commit range, not file lists.
- Keep briefs short and point to files; check the usage report after each checkpoint and cut what re-reads the same files.

## Handoffs: cold starts and token efficiency

Side agents start with **no memory of the conversation**. Every handoff carries exactly what they need and nothing more.

**Orchestrator, when handing off:**
- Pass **file paths and decision IDs, not pasted contents.** The agent reads what it needs.
- Name the **minimum reading list** (usually 1-3 files plus the relevant IDs). Never tell a builder to read all of `docs/` or `guidelines/`; the rules a builder needs are in this file.
- State the **scope as a whitelist of files** it may create or edit, and what is out of bounds.
- Give **checkable acceptance criteria** (a test passes, `pnpm check` is green, a specific behavior).
- One task per brief, small enough to finish in one pass. Split large work into independent briefs with no shared files, each step building and passing checks before the next.
- Ask for a **short, structured return** so the result is cheap to read back.

**Brief template:**

```
Task: <one sentence>
Why: <decision IDs, e.g. D4, T5>
Read first: <paths, max ~3>
May edit/create: <file whitelist>
Do not touch: <paths or areas>
Done when: <checkable criteria; include `pnpm check` green>
Return: files changed, one line per change, anything unresolved. No code dumps.
```

**Builder, on start:** read the brief, then only the listed files; do not explore the repo or re-read docs unless told. Follow neighboring patterns. Do not widen scope; note adjacent problems in the return instead of fixing them. Run `pnpm check` before returning and report failures verbatim and briefly.

**Reviewer (Opus), on start:** receive the diff and the decision IDs it should satisfy, not the history. Check against these rules and the cited IDs; report findings ranked by severity with file and line. Do not rewrite code.

**Return format (all side agents):**

```
Status: done | blocked | partial
Changed: <path>: <what, one line>
Checks: <pnpm check result>
Open: <questions, risks, follow-ups>
```

## Context hygiene

- Keep this file and the briefs short; long context costs tokens on every cold start.
- Record durable decisions in `docs/` (with an ID), not in chat. A decision that exists only in a conversation is lost to the next agent.
- When a rule here changes, update this file in the same change.

## Git

Work on `development`; `main` is for releases. Short, imperative commit messages. One commit per change; update any doc the change touches. Add one dependency or one upgrade per commit. The raw AI session files in `ai-sessions/` are added last, unedited except for masked secrets, as the brief requires.
